name: Salicaceae

lineage_context.teaching_goal: For the local Salix/Populus pool, teach dioecious catkins, a 1-locular ovary with parietal placentation, and capsules releasing many comose seeds.

project_scope.selection_mode: Central Texas Salix + Populus family module
project_scope.note: The modern broad Salicaceae is diverse, but the project pool is entirely the classic temperate Salix/Populus branch, so the visual lesson centers on that architecture.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: On a woody plant, look for unisexual catkins. In female flowers, confirm a single superior 1-locular ovary with parietal placentation; the fruit becomes a 2–4-valved capsule packed with many tiny seeds bearing long silky hairs.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Trees or shrubs with alternate simple leaves and usually small deciduous stipules. Local Salix leaves tend narrower; Populus leaves are broader and buds have several visible outer scales.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Plants are dioecious in the local pool. Flowers are extremely reduced and packed into catkins; perianth is absent in Salix and Populus, with one or more nectary/disc glands present.
family_diagnostics.fruit: A dry capsule opening by 2–4 valves and releasing numerous minute seeds with a conspicuous coma of long hairs.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Catkin + one-celled parietal ovary + cottony seed capsule is the local Salicaceae machine.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: catkin → naked unisexual flower → 1-locular/parietal ovary → capsule + cottony seeds → Salix-vs-Populus
visual_lesson.intro: Willows and cottonwoods are not just 'catkin trees.' Their best confirmation is what the female catkin turns into: a one-celled capsule full of silky-haired seeds.

steps.title: 1 · Start with the catkin
steps.look_for: Dense unisexual catkins on a woody plant, often before or with expanding leaves.
steps.why_it_matters: Moves immediately toward the classic Salix/Populus branch of Salicaceae.

steps.title: 2 · Notice how reduced each flower is
steps.look_for: No ordinary petals or sepals in local Salix/Populus; each flower is subtended by a bract and accompanied by nectary/disc tissue.
steps.why_it_matters: Explains why these flowers look unlike most showy Malpighiales.

steps.title: 3 · Read the female ovary
steps.look_for: One chamber with multiple ovules borne on parietal placentas rather than three closed locules around a center.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the high-value split from Euphorbiaceae and Phyllanthaceae.

steps.title: 4 · Confirm with cottony seeds
steps.look_for: A dry capsule opening into valves and releasing many tiny seeds carried by long silky hairs.
steps.why_it_matters: One of the most memorable family-level fruit/seed characters in the whole project.

steps.title: 5 · Salix vs Populus
steps.look_for: Salix usually has a single outer bud scale and narrower leaves; Populus has several bud scales, broader mature leaves and different catkin proportions.
steps.why_it_matters: Cleanly hands family recognition into the project's two genera.

comparisons.title: Salicaceae vs Phyllanthaceae
comparisons.rule: Salicaceae female flowers have a 1-locular ovary with parietal placentation and many ovules; Phyllanthaceae commonly has a multi-locular ovary with two ovules per locule and a schizocarp/columella fruit plan.

comparisons.title: Salicaceae vs Euphorbiaceae
comparisons.rule: Euphorbiaceae commonly has a 3-locular ovary with one ovule per locule and a central columella; local Salix/Populus has one chamber with parietal placentas and many ovules.

comparisons.title: Salicaceae vs Betulaceae/Fagaceae-style catkins
comparisons.rule: Catkins alone are not enough. Salix/Populus confirm with their naked flowers, one-celled parietal ovary and silky-haired capsule seeds.

visual_lesson.caveat: Modern Salicaceae includes many former Flacourtiaceae genera that do not look like Salix or Populus. This module is explicitly the project's local Salix/Populus door.

genera.fast_cue: narrower leaves + one outer bud scale + willow catkins + cottony seed capsules
broader mature leaves + several bud scales + cottonwood catkins/capsules

taxonomy_notes: Populus deltoides subsp. deltoides is an accepted infraspecific taxon under current Kew; keep it distinct from the species-level source row without treating them as unrelated species.

visual_targets.annotation_goal: show one chamber and parietal placentation
label valves and silky seed hairs
one outer scale vs several scales
parietal one chamber vs axile multi-locular
